review_notes: I read the whole target file and diffed it against its two sibling files by grep and a partial read. I found no repeated reasoning inside this file that is worth extracting; the repeated `rw [← hj₀ a]; simp` steps are too short. The real duplication is across three files. The base file, `_of_eq_two` and `_of_eq_three` share the same three helper lemmas at lines 25–79. They also share the same main-proof tail from `hymap` at line 192 to the end. In the `_three` file the grep shows the same line numbers for `hymap`, `hjres`, `hdiff` and `hresa`. The only difference I confirmed is the imported and called descent theorem (`..._of_eq_two` versus `..._of_eq_three`, with `hq2` versus `hq3`). I did not read the tail of the `_three` file or the base file line by line, so I can't be sure they are textually identical. I also did not check the other `charP_residueField` copies in the repo (some have different hypotheses), so I left them out. I can't run Lean, so the proposed shared lemmas are untested. The signatures are sketched from the hypotheses actually used in the proof.

findings.problem: The three general helper lemmas have no dependence on q = 2. Each is copy-pasted verbatim, with the same names and proofs, into the sibling files `..._descent.lean` and `..._descent_of_eq_three.lean`. `exists_ringHom_residueField_comp_eq` is about 25 lines and builds an `IsLocalHom` instance and a residue-field `RingEquiv`. `mem_maximalIdeal_of_algebraMap_mem_maximalIdeal` is a non-trivial unit-inverse argument. A fix or generalisation has to be made in three places.
findings.proposed_change: Move the three lemmas unchanged into one shared definitions/util file, for example `Definitions/Def_ValuationSubring_ResidueHelpers.lean` or `P2M.Util`, under one namespace. The shared file needs no imports beyond Mathlib. The statements are unchanged: `charP_residueField (q) [Fact q.Prime] (A : ValuationSubring (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)) (hA : A.LiesOverPrime q) : CharP (ResidueField ↥A) q`; `mem_maximalIdeal_of_algebraMap_mem_maximalIdeal (A O hO x h) : x ∈ maximalIdeal ↥A`; and `exists_ringHom_residueField_comp_eq ι hres ϖ₀ hϖ₀ ψ hψ`. Each of the three solution files then imports it and deletes the `namespace SSConvDrinfeldCentre` block (lines 21–83 here). The call sites are unchanged: `SSConvDrinfeldCentre.charP_residueField q A hA`, `SSConvDrinfeldCentre.mem_maximalIdeal_of_algebraMap_mem_maximalIdeal A (OSS s) (hSS_A s)` and `SSConvDrinfeldCentre.exists_ringHom_residueField_comp_eq ι hres ϖ₀ hϖ₀ (φ.comp …) hψϖ`. Only the namespace prefix changes if the shared file uses another name.
findings.benefit: Each lemma is stated and proved once, so a fix is made in one place, and each solution file shrinks by about 60 lines. The reader of this file reaches the genuinely q=2-specific argument sooner.

findings.problem: After the single call to the q=2 descent theorem, the rest of the proof (lines 192–276) does not use `hq2`. That includes the `jqModC` reduction facts `hymap`, `hjint` and `hjres`, the supersingular-place bookkeeping `hsW`/`hconst`, and the maximal-ideal difference argument `hdiff`/`hresa`. It also includes the `hψϖ`/`θ` transfer through `φ`. The sibling file `..._of_eq_three.lean` has the same blocks at the same line numbers (`hymap` at 192, `hjres` at 207, `hdiff` at 240, `hresa` at 263). Only the called theorem (`..._descent_of_eq_two` versus `..._of_eq_three`) differs. So about 85 lines of non-trivial reasoning are duplicated, and the same applies to the base `..._descent.lean`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a shared lemma, for example `mem_ssJSet_of_exists_jInvariant_sub_mem`. Its hypotheses are exactly those the tail uses: `hA`, `hW`, `hle`, `R₀`, `hR₀`, `hSS_A`, `hSS_over`, `ι`, `hres`, `ϖ₀`, `hϖ₀`, `F₀`, `hjF₀`, `hj₀`, `𝔫`, `hϖ`, `hs`, `φ`, `hφ`, `s`.
